post_text:
I insisted on strict schema validation for our internal microservices when we were still small.

While the rest of the team pushed for "flexible" JSON blobs to maintain velocity, I chose Protobuf and a central schema registry. 🛡️

Nothing crashed. Everything degraded.

At the time, it felt unnecessarily rigid. The frontend leads hated the extra build step, and the "move fast" advocates argued that a shared registry created a bottleneck for simple feature additions. They wanted the freedom to iterate without a formal contract review for every minor field change. It was a conservative choice that felt like a speed bump in a race.

Two years later, our engineering department tripled in size. A developer in a different time zone pushed a breaking change to the core billing service, renaming a critical field. Because of the registry, the CI pipeline blocked the merge immediately. It caught the mismatch before a single byte reached the staging environment. No production outage occurred, and no one had to stay up until 3 AM debugging a "null" value.

We didn't need a post-mortem or a hero to save the day. The boring choice I made years prior simply did its job in silence. ☕

What I learned:

Boring contracts prevent exciting failures.
